draft.title: Accuracy, precision and reproducibility
card: Results are close to the true value. A measurement of 100 mL of water that reads 99.8 mL is accurate.
Results are close to each other, whether or not they are close to the true value. Repeat readings of 95.1, 95.0 and 95.2 mL are precise.
Other people repeat the same method and get results that agree with the first set. This makes the findings more trustworthy.
A set of results can be precise but not accurate, if all the readings sit close together but away from the true value.
draft.remember: Accurate: near the true value. Precise: near each other. Reproducible: others get the same.

a.q: A student weighs a 50.0 g mass four times and gets 56.2 g, 56.3 g, 56.2 g and 56.3 g. How can these results be described?
a.why: The readings are very close to each other, so they are precise. They are all well above 50.0 g, so they are not close to the true value and are not accurate. Being close together does not make results accurate.
a.clue: Compare the readings with each other, then with 50.0 g.

b.q: Priya finds that a plant grows 4.1 cm in a week under a red light. Three other student groups follow her method and each find about 4 cm. What does this show?
opts: Her results are free of error
b.why: Other groups followed the same method and got results that agree with hers, so the results are reproducible. Precision is about how close repeat readings are within one set of measurements. Agreement alone does not show the results are close to a true value.
b.clue: Who repeated the method, and did they agree?
